## The question

In 2014, the Affordable Care Act offered states the option of expanding Medicaid coverage
and opened the Marketplace for private insurance. As a result, total Medicaid spending in
expansion states increased.

We investigate what happened to enrollment, spending and utilization during Medicaid expansion
for Medicaid, Medicare, and private insurance across states.

## Data and design

IHME Disease Expenditure Project (DEX): state-level spending and encounters by payer
and setting, 2010--2018. Uninsurance from CPS.

Difference-in-differences comparing the **25 states that expanded on 1 January 2014** with
the **19 that never expanded**. Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) group-time estimator,
never-treated controls, adjusting for poverty, median income, pre-expansion uninsurance and
age structure. Standard errors clustered by state, multiplier bootstrap.

```{=typst}
#note[Later-expanding cohorts are excluded due to small sample size (n ≤ 3 each year).]
```

## 1. Expansion covered the uninsured

![](figures/f1_coverage.png)

```{=typst}
#note[Teal: the 25 states that expanded in 2014. Amber: the 19 that never expanded.]
```

| Coverage | Effect | 95% CI | Pre-test |
|:---------|-------:|:-------|---------:|
| Medicaid  | +3.69 | [+2.27, +5.12] | 0.84 |
| Medicare  | −0.20 | [−0.54, +0.14] | 0.72 |
| Uninsured | −1.38 | [−2.48, −0.28] | 0.30 |
| Private   | −2.16 | [−3.07, −1.24] | 0.96 |

Medicaid rose **3.7 points**. The uninsured rate fell **1.4 points** further than in control
states. Private insurance increased with the Marketplace in both settings, to a greater extent in non-expansion states.

```{=typst}
#colbreak()
```

### 2. New enrollees had similar healthcare consumption

![](figures/f2_medicaid.png)

```{=typst}
#note[Difference-in-differences effect at each year relative to 2014, as a percentage of the pre-expansion level in expansion states. Points left of the dashed line are the parallel-trends pre-test made visible. 95% intervals.]
```

Enrollment rose **19.9%** and spending per resident rose **18.0%** (SE 3.9). Spending per
enrollee did not follow: **−3.3%** (SE 4.4).

Against a pre-expansion **$5,649** per enrollee, the marginal enrollee cost roughly
**$4,500** per year.

### 3. Private insurance did not shrink to pay for it

![](figures/f3_private.png)

**Private coverage rose in both groups** --- 62.9 to 64.4% in expanders, 62.6 to 66.5% in
controls. The −2.2 point estimate is control states gaining faster, not expansion states
losing. Marketplace subsidies cover 100--138% FPL where Medicaid does not.

Private spending per enrollee **+4.8%** (SE 2.8) and per resident **+1.7%** (SE 2.4).
Neither reaches significance. Spending did not fall on either margin.

Encounters per enrollee are positive in all five settings (**+2.2 to +5.6%**) and
significant in none, so what movement there is looks like **use rather than price**. The
most likely reading is dilution of the *control* group's risk pool as lower-utilising
marketplace enrollees joined it.

```{=typst}
#note[Axes as in panel 2. Encounters are not summed across settings: a prescription fill and a hospital stay are not the same unit.]
```

```{=typst}
#colbreak()
```

## 4. Nothing else moved

Medicare spending per resident **+0.4%** (SE 1.3) --- nothing, on any margin. Private
spending per resident **+1.7%** (SE 2.4).

Of the **36 spending estimates** below, three survive correction for multiple comparisons,
and all three are Medicaid spending per resident. Among the **24 non-Medicaid** estimates,
one clears 5% before correction and **none survives it**.

**Spending per resident**

| Setting | Medicaid | Medicare | Private |
|:--------|---------:|---------:|--------:|
| All care    | +18.0 (3.9) * |  +0.4 (1.3) | +1.7 (2.4) |
| Ambulatory  | +23.6 (5.8) * |  −0.9 (1.2) | +2.1 (2.4) |
| Emergency   | +21.7 (8.1)   |  +2.9 (4.9) | −0.2 (1.9) |
| Inpatient   | +22.5 (4.5) * |  +0.5 (1.4) | +1.2 (3.4) |
| Nursing     |  +2.0 (6.9)   |  +3.0 (5.6) | +4.6 (7.2) |
| Pharmacy    | +11.1 (12.8)  |  +0.8 (2.9) | +0.8 (5.2) |

**Spending per enrollee**

| Setting | Medicaid | Medicare | Private |
|:--------|---------:|---------:|--------:|
| All care    |  −3.3 (4.4)  | +1.5 (0.8) | +4.8 (2.8) |
| Ambulatory  |  +0.0 (6.2)  | +0.9 (0.8) | +5.3 (3.0) |
| Emergency   |  −2.0 (7.8)  | +3.8 (2.7) | +3.2 (2.2) |
| Inpatient   |  +4.4 (4.9)  | +0.8 (0.9) | +4.0 (3.6) |
| Nursing     | −14.4 (9.7)  | +4.1 (4.9) | +7.3 (7.3) |
| Pharmacy    | −22.5 (18.0) | +3.2 (1.4) | +4.2 (4.7) |

```{=typst}
#note[Effect as % of the pre-2014 level (SE). \* survives Benjamini--Hochberg correction across the 36 estimates. Every Medicaid model passes the parallel-trends pre-test; private is borderline at $p = 0.07$.]
```

## Limitations

Estimates describe 2014 expanders and non-expanders only.

**Out-of-pocket spending is not included in analysis.** Uninsured spending
and out-of-pocket deductibles or copays for the insured cannot be distinguished in DEX.

Private coverage changes cannot be attributed to individual switching.
